lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Council, I'd like to call this meeting to order. Welcome here, everyone. At this time, I would like to give the opening to Councillor Damian Penner.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. If any of your social media feeds were similar to mine, this last week had my pages all full of discussions about tariffs, trade wars, and international relations. In response to the rhetoric we were hearing regarding the potential for tariffs, many news outlets and individuals began discussing how to support local, which national brands were either Canadian or operated within Canada, and ways to support businesses and companies that are from our great nation. While I am not overjoyed with the reasons why this conversation came to the forefront of Canadians' thoughts and discussions, I do hope that the reflection on how we can support Canadian and local businesses remains in the memories of the consumer for a long time to come. Supporting local has a generational impact on communities. And while it can sometimes come at a higher cost to the consumer at the initial purchase, the long-term savings and investment into the community often balances the scale into a net-zero impact, if not a savings in a lifetime. Supporting local has numerous benefits to your community, your fellow neighbour, and the future health of the city for not only yourself, but for your children and family. Generally, local businesses are considered small businesses. Having said that, these small businesses employ over 60% of All workers in Canada. Having a healthy small business community drives commerce, employment, and tax revenue to maintain a healthy city and region. Small businesses are the backbone to our economy and help drive it forward by opening up employment opportunities for individuals looking to work at places other than big box stores. Often in small businesses, you find a more personal work experience with a stronger purpose while working right alongside the owner and those personally invested into the success of the business. and in turn, the individuals that they employ. Every transaction at a local business is not taken for granted, but instead cherished and appreciated. Small businesses also are not just all about themselves. When you see a small business owner— or pardon me, when you see a small business and the owner working inside of the establishment, you know where your funds are going. While a box of cereal bought at one store versus another may be the exact same product, But when you support a local business, you are helping a family that has invested their time, energy, and funds into our local economy, often also purchasing their products locally to support their neighbours and the many individuals they employ. Small businesses also are more likely to help support community events, local charities, and sponsorships to the organizations that matter to you locally. According to Forbes, small businesses donate 250% more than large businesses to local nonprofits, community, and community causes, creating a positive cycle of giving back locally. Local small businesses are also much more likely to offer unique and culturally specific items that you cannot find at big box stores. In order to stand out, small businesses often are more innovative and unique in their offerings. Without a large national marketing strategy, these local shops rely on strong customer service, products that are targeted directly to the local demographics, and and new unique offerings that you may not have seen before or even knew existed. Often many small businesses operating in the same or similar industry can thrive in the same community, whereas a community is limited in how many big box stores it can support. A multitude of small businesses, each selecting products based not on national sales plans but on their own interests and the needs of the local customers, guarantees a much broader range of product choices. The term support local can be a popular catchphrase used by local governments, chambers of commerce, and small business advocates. However, the conversations of how to support local and how important it is on a national scale needs to make this popular catchphrase evolve from a theoretical benefit and something that— and something that's nice to say to make yourself feel good, and instead into a daily practice of your spending habits. Thank you.

lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is a public hearing for the city's 2025 Local Improvement Plan 2025-01, as you mentioned, which is a force main twinning project that will extend from the city's existing lift station on Park Road West approximately 3 kilometers to its wastewater sewage lagoon located west of Steinbach. Total costs of this project are estimated to be $6.5 million. $6.595 million to be financed with a borrowing of a maximum of $2.75 million. That borrowing is planned to be repaid over a 5-year period with a maximum annual interest rate of 7%, resulting in an annual repayment of just under $670,700. The remaining project costs are to be funded by the city's utility reserve fund, utility operating fund, and an expected grant funding from either provincial or federal sources. The equivalent mill rate for the proposed borrowing and repayment will be approximately 0.488 mills. And what that means to the annual or to the average residential taxpayer with a home valued at $250,000 will be a tax impact of just under $50. $155 per year. The notices as are required under the Municipal Act have been issued. There is no written correspondence on the file. Recommendation from city council is subject to any further information that may be provided that both first reading and second reading to Local Improvement Plan 2025-01 And local improvement bylaw 2255 be provided.

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. The special service plan 2025-01 and bylaw 2257 Thank you. bylaws 2015-57 represent a proposed rate program for the city's residential curbside waste collection system. This is a bylaw that the city has passed in over many successive years. Typically, it does get proposed on a 3 or a 4-year rate plan depending on the needs of the city. Special service plan is being proposed for rates that will affect 2025, 2026, and 2027, and specifically for all residential properties within the city of Steinbach. Notices as are required under the Municipal Act were issued. There is no written correspondence on file. The the special service plan is intended to raise sufficient revenues to pay for the costs of the. And the estimated cost per resident under this bylaw will be set at $162 in 2025, $168 in 2026, and $174 in 2027. The current rate per household in 2024 was set at $155, and from an From an annual increase perspective, year 1 would see an increase of 4.5% or $7 per year, year 2, 3.7% or $6 per year, and year 3, 3.6% or $6 per year. Recommendation from administration is that council give this bylaw first and second readings.

Nothing is being changed in regards to the service that we're providing. lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Mr. Mayor and members of council, I do have the information to follow. It is I have a presentation in the form of a PowerPoint, so while you don't have any handouts in your agenda package, it is information I'll present on screen. The city is proceeding into its 3rd calendar year in event centre construction. I'm somewhat reluctant to say it that way, but it is a large and very significant project, and It does take an enormous effort to get it completed. The good news is, based on latest information, we do expect to have occupancy of the facility by March of this year, and that is just around the corner. Just to give council a bit of an update as to where things are at, I've got some images of the exterior of the building. Nearly all of the exterior and site works, at least as far as the west parking lot being the main entrance at the corner of Elmdale Street and Reimer Avenue, were completed before winter conditions set in in the fall of 2024. The parking lot in this area was completed. The landscaping was completed. However, as you can see, there are still some minor areas of the building Yes. The exterior of the building, particularly where the new building ties into the existing T.G. Smith Rink, is concerned. Other than that, there are generally small areas around the exterior of the building that still need to be completed, and that would include the exterior signage for the building, which will be coming up in the next few 2 weeks. Included with the exterior of the building is the exit stairs. There are some fairly significant exit stairs on the Hanover, Hanover Street side of the building. Those have been in progress for some time. This picture that you're seeing on the screen was taken 2 weeks ago. There has been continued progress being made, and the railings have now been are now being started for those exit stairs. On the interior of the building, I'll start with the least exciting spaces first. So that would be the locker rooms and the restrooms. The progress on the locker rooms and change rooms, those are probably the furthest ahead with most of the fixtures and finishing completed. I've got an image there of a typical locker room. The paint is completed. The washroom areas and showers are generally complete within those. The public change— sorry, the public washroom areas are still in progress. However, there's been significant work with plumbing fixtures being installed in those. The club zone, which includes the suites, are making significant progress. You can see the image on the left There is a significant degree of the glass barriers and partitions that have been installed. The millwork is also starting to be installed in those areas. The general concourse, including the pistons gear shop, is mostly complete. There's also been further work on putting together the mounting Yes. And the areas for the score clocks and general millwork and fixtures continue to be put in as well. As far as the media area of the arena bowl, that is that— we call it level 300. You'll see some of that painting that has been done on the exterior of that media box area. There's still a fair bit to go for the interior finishing, but primarily made up of final fixtures and millwork. As far as the arena bowl, that has also seen significant progress. Probably the most dramatic over the past few weeks is that the actual Okay. Ice surface lighting has been turned on and you can see it in the image that's on screen. There continues to be significant work in connecting AV structure or project equipment that's required within the arena bowl area, significant millwork and other general fixtures. Based on the schedule, the rink floor cooldown process is anticipated to begin Next week, Monday, February 10th. It takes about a week to slowly bring the temperature of that arena floor down so that all of the systems and the materials can assimilate to that change in temperature. And once that process is complete, then the making of the ice surface may begin. And right now that is scheduled to begin the week of February 17th. Thank you. Thank you. As far as the atrium, the primary stairway leading from the entryway and main level up to the 2nd floor concourse area to gain access into the arena bowl is nearly complete. And you also see another image on the right-hand side. It too was taken about a week and a half ago, and generally all of the railings and And much of the painting is complete with the majority of the remaining work required for fixtures and paint— final painting and making connections within the kitchen area. Overall, as of December 31st, total billings, progress billings for the project are just under $61.6 million. Million, of which in the last quarter of 2024 amounted to about $11.8 million in total. Included in that number are total change orders of just over $8.3 million as of December 24th or December 31st. That again is what was generally anticipated. when the project began. And finally, just a couple of images of— top left is an image of the facility that was taken in October of 2024. And then the bottom right, that is a screenshot of the exterior of the building that was taken as of this morning. So generally, as I said, we are anticipating gaining occupancy and access to the facility in March, and crews are continuing to work diligently to make sure that we are able to access the building at that time.
